function_question: Why can AI be unfair, and how do we fix it?

opening.text: There was a proud robot called Pixel whose new fruit sorter had just passed its test.
Pixel sorted fruit in the school kitchen, but it kept calling green apples "not apples".
Pixel wondered: "I'm not broken. So what did I secretly learn from my examples?"

card.goal: Find the bias and fix it

chapters.label: Chapter 1
chapters.title: The green apple mystery
chapters.line: Pixel passed its test, so why does it keep saying green apples aren't apples?

chapters.label: Chapter 2
chapters.title: Pixel asks for help
chapters.line: Pixel needs a detective on the team. What about you?

chapters.label: Chapter 3
chapters.title: Real-world blind spots
chapters.line: You and Pixel find out how other AIs learned something unfair.

chapters.label: Chapter 4
chapters.title: The secret of fair data
chapters.line: An AI is only as fair as its examples.

chapters.label: Chapter 5
chapters.title: The red-apple lab
chapters.line: No magic, just cards! Build a sorter that has only ever seen red apples.

chapters.label: Chapter 5½
chapters.title: Digging for the root
chapters.line: Why? And why again? Keep digging until you hit the real cause.

chapters.label: Chapter 6
chapters.title: The fair test plan
chapters.line: One row for every group, so nobody gets missed.

chapters.label: Chapter 7
chapters.title: Group by group
chapters.line: Test each group, add the missing examples, and test again.

chapters.label: Chapter 8
chapters.title: Fair for every apple
chapters.line: Pixel knows a green apple is still an apple.

guide.brief: I'm Popi, your story guide. Pixel isn't broken, but it learned something unfair from its examples. Can you help Pixel find its blind spot, prove it with data, and fix it? Let's start!
guide.your_idea: Some detectives already have a hunch. Do you?
guide.nature_clues: Bias happens when an AI learns from one-sided examples. Tap each card to see it in the real world!
guide.design_secret: Here's the secret behind every blind spot…
guide.skill: Unplugged first! Your card sorter has only seen red apples. Which group will it sort best? Predict, then test.
guide.sketch: Time to plan a fair test like a real AI fairness team!
guide.build_and_test: Test Pixel on each group separately. Which group does worst?
guide.retry_tip: Add the MISSING examples, not just more of the same, then test every group again!
guide.ending: And ever since then, Pixel sorts every apple fairly, red or green, because YOU found its blind spot and fixed the data!

quick_check.question: Pixel gets 9 of 10 red apples right, but only 2 of 10 green apples. Which group does worst?
quick_check.right: Yes! 20% against 90%. Testing each group separately is how you catch a blind spot.
quick_check.wrong: Not quite. Which group got fewer right out of 10?

clue_cards.name: Early face detectors
clue_cards.trick: They were trained mostly on lighter-skinned faces.
clue_cards.does: They worked worse for people with darker skin.

clue_cards.name: Voice assistants
clue_cards.trick: They heard fewer examples of some accents while learning.
clue_cards.does: They often struggled to understand those accents.

clue_cards.name: Husky-or-wolf sorter
clue_cards.trick: Its wolf photos nearly always had snow in the background.
clue_cards.does: It learned "snow means wolf" instead of looking at the animal.

clue_cards.name: Fair AI teams
clue_cards.trick: They test their systems on every group of users.
clue_cards.does: When one group gets worse results, they fix the data.

predict.prompt: Fair or unfair training data for an apple sorter? Predict first!

items.label: Apples always on a white plate

predict.explain: One-sided data teaches a secret shortcut: red apples only teaches "apple = red", and a white plate every time teaches "plate = apple", just like the husky-or-wolf snow cheat.

lab.title: The red-apple lab
lab.predict: Your card sorter only learned from red apples. Which group will it sort best?

tool.name: 5 Whys
tool.intro: 5 Whys is a detective tool: ask why, then ask why about the answer, again and again. Today you'll use all 5 whys to reach the root cause.

parts.name: Why #1
parts.example: 🪴 Why is my plant drooping? It's thirsty.
parts.starter: Why does Pixel call a green apple "not an apple"? Because…

parts.name: Why #2
parts.what: Ask why again, one level deeper.
parts.example: 🪴 Why is it thirsty? The soil is dry.
parts.starter: Why does Pixel think an apple must be red? Because…

parts.name: Why #3
parts.example: 🪴 Why is the soil dry? Nobody watered it.
parts.starter: Why did Pixel learn "apple = red"? Because…

parts.name: Why #4
parts.what: Don't stop at the first easy answer.
parts.example: 🪴 Why did nobody water it? We forgot it was there.
parts.starter: Why did Pixel only see red apples? Because…

parts.name: Why #5
parts.what: Reach the root cause you can fix.
parts.example: 🪴 Why did we forget? It hides behind the curtain. Move it!
parts.starter: Why was the training data one-sided? Because…
